subject: Literacy
title: Animal sounds
objectives: Children will match animal pictures to sounds.
Children will make animal sounds and say the animal name.
content: Farm animals and their sounds, birds and insects, and games that match animal pictures to sounds.
teachingActivities: Use real familiar Nigerian animals such as goat, hen, dog, cat and cow; say the name first, then make the sound; let children make the sound before you show the picture.
learnerActivities: Name animals, make animal sounds, match pictures to sounds and join animal sound games.
resources: Large pictures of a goat, hen, dog, cat, cow and bird
A recording of animal sounds if available
assessment: Observe whether each child names at least three animals and makes at least one animal sound.
expectedOutcomes: Makes the sound of a familiar animal.

lessons.title: Farm friends
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name three farm animals and make their sounds.
successCriteria: Names or points to a goat, a hen and a dog
Makes the sound of at least one animal
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make loud and quiet sounds and use their voices in play, such as brum for a car.
resources: Large pictures of a goat, hen and dog
lessons.starter: Take the goat picture from the basket and say "Meh, meh. This is a goat." Ask "What does the goat say?"
teacherActivities: Show the goat picture, say its name and make its sound. Repeat with the hen ("cluck") and the dog ("woof").
Say a sound and ask "Which animal is it?"
Say an animal name and ask the children to make its sound.
Give each child a picture to hold and call out the sound.
learnerActivities: Children look, point and copy each sound.
Children point to the matching picture.
Children make the sound.
Child holds up the animal when they hear the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the goat picture, say its name and make its sound. Repeat with the hen ("cluck") and the dog ("woof"). Children: Children look, point and copy each sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a sound and ask "Which animal is it?" Children: Children point to the matching picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Say an animal name and ask the children to make its sound. Children: Children make the sound.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a picture to hold and call out the sound. Children: Child holds up the animal when they hear the sound.

practical.title: Animal baskets
steps: Place three animal toys or pictures in a basket.
Each child picks one and says or shows its name.
The group makes the animal’s sound together.
practical.safety: Use clean toys and pictures. Remind children to be gentle with animals and to wash hands after real animals.

differentiation.support: Offer two animals and make the sound with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose an animal and say what it eats.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names or points to three animals
lessons.conclusion: Put each picture back in the basket and say its name and sound.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to make the sound of a goat, a hen or a dog at home or outside.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name three farm animals and make their sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The goat says meh, meh, meh. The hen says cluck, cluck, cluck.

lessons.title: Cat, cow and bird
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name a cat, a cow and a bird and make their sounds.
successCriteria: Names or points to a cat, a cow and a bird
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make loud and quiet sounds and use their voices in play, such as brum for a car.
resources: Pictures of a cat, a cow and a bird
lessons.starter: Hold up the soft toy cat and stroke it gently. Say "Meow, meow. What does the cat say?"
teacherActivities: Show the cat and say "Meow". Show the cow and say "Moo". Show the bird and say "Tweet".
Hide a picture behind your back and make its sound. Ask "Which animal?"
Say "Fly like a bird" and flap your arms. Say "Walk like a cow."
Let each child pick a card and make the animal sound.
learnerActivities: Children point and make each sound.
Children point to the picture they think it is.
Children move like each animal.
Child shows the card and makes the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the cat and say "Meow". Show the cow and say "Moo". Show the bird and say "Tweet". Children: Children point and make each sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Hide a picture behind your back and make its sound. Ask "Which animal?" Children: Children point to the picture they think it is.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Fly like a bird" and flap your arms. Say "Walk like a cow." Children: Children move like each animal.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a card and make the animal sound. Children: Child shows the card and makes the sound.

practical.title: Move like an animal
steps: Clear a space on the mat.
Call "bird", "cat" or "cow" and everyone moves like that animal.
Say "freeze" and listen for one sound.
practical.safety: Clear the floor of toys and keep children well apart. Stop the game if anyone looks tired.

differentiation.support: Use two pictures and move beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the group in an animal move and sound.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Moves and sounds like an animal
lessons.conclusion: Fold your wings and settle on the mat like a bird going to sleep.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at pictures of animals in a book or outside and say each sound with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name a cat, a cow and a bird and make their sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Bees, ants and a story
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will listen for small animal sounds in a short story.
successCriteria: Points to the bee or the ant in a picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make loud and quiet sounds and use their voices in play, such as brum for a car.
resources: A picture of a bee and an ant
lessons.starter: Wave the yellow scarf and say "Bzzz. A bee is flying." Ask the children "Can you buzz?"
teacherActivities: Show the bee picture and say "Bzzz, bee". Show the ant and say "Tiny ant."
Tell a short story: "A bee flew to a flower. Bzzz. The bee went home." Use the scarf.
Ask "Where is the bee?" and "Where is the ant?"
Give each child a turn to fly the scarf bee while others buzz.
learnerActivities: Children buzz and hold up a finger for tiny.
Children buzz and follow the scarf with their eyes.
Children point to the pictures.
Child flies the scarf and friends buzz.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the bee picture and say "Bzzz, bee". Show the ant and say "Tiny ant." Children: Children buzz and hold up a finger for tiny.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell a short story: "A bee flew to a flower. Bzzz. The bee went home." Use the scarf. Children: Children buzz and follow the scarf with their eyes.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where is the bee?" and "Where is the ant?" Children: Children point to the pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a turn to fly the scarf bee while others buzz. Children: Child flies the scarf and friends buzz.

practical.title: Buzzing bees
steps: Give each child a scarf or a paper bee.
Walk slowly around the mat buzzing like a bee.
When you say "flower", everyone sits and stops buzzing.
practical.safety: Keep an adult watching for falls and remove sharp items. Tell children that real bees and ants are looked at, not touched.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s scarf and buzz together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what the bee did in the story.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the ant big or tiny?

expectedOutcomes: Joins in animal sounds in a story
Points to a bee or an ant
lessons.conclusion: Let the bee fly home and say "Goodnight bee."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for an ant or a bird outside and say its name and sound with your child, without touching.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen for small animal sounds in a short story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Animal sound games
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will match six animal pictures to their sounds in a game.
successCriteria: Matches a sound to an animal picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make loud and quiet sounds and use their voices in play, such as brum for a car.
resources: Six animal pictures: goat, hen, dog, cat, cow, bird
lessons.starter: Say "I am thinking of an animal. Meh, meh, meh. Who am I?" Let the children point to the goat.
teacherActivities: Lay out the six pictures. Make one sound and ask the children to point to the animal.
Say a name and ask the children to make the sound.
Play "Which animal is missing?" by hiding one picture.
Let each child hide a picture and play with a friend.
learnerActivities: Children point to the matching picture.
Children make the sound.
Children look and point to the empty space or name the animal.
Child hides, friend guesses.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Lay out the six pictures. Make one sound and ask the children to point to the animal. Children: Children point to the matching picture.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a name and ask the children to make the sound. Children: Children make the sound.
Step 3. Teacher: Play "Which animal is missing?" by hiding one picture. Children: Children look and point to the empty space or name the animal.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hide a picture and play with a friend. Children: Child hides, friend guesses.

practical.title: Animal lotto
steps: Place six pictures on the mat.
Children take turns to touch the animal that makes the sound.
practical.safety: Use large pictures and keep small pieces away from mouths. Supervise sharing and turns.

differentiation.support: Use three pictures and make the sound slowly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a sound for a friend to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to each animal and say its name.
lessons.homeConnection: Make an animal sound at home and ask your child to say which animal it is.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match six animal pictures to their sounds in a game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 animal check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe which animals each child can name and which sounds they can make.
successCriteria: Makes at least one animal sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make loud and quiet sounds and use their voices in play, such as brum for a car.
lessons.starter: Sing the animal song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: picture matching, animal toys and animal moves.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "What does it say?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child names the animal or makes the sound.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: picture matching, animal toys and animal moves. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "What does it say?" Children: Child names the animal or makes the sound.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Animal stations
practical.safety: Use soft toys and large pictures only. Keep floors clear and supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to choose an animal and teach a friend its sound.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names animals; makes animal sounds; matches a sound to a picture.

questions.question: What is this animal?
questions.expected: Goat, hen, dog, cat, cow or bird.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
Names and makes sounds of familiar animals
lessons.conclusion: Sing "The goat says meh" and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to name the animals they see at home or on the street.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe which animals each child can name and which sounds they can make" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
